weights.weightCitation: Baveno VII (de Franchis R et al., J Hepatol 2022); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). Large-volume haematemesis +/- melaena in portal hypertension (cirrhotic — jaundice/ascites; or schistosomal — see that entry). Resuscitate + terlipressin/octreotide + prophylactic antibiotics + urgent endoscopic band ligation. UGANDA: HBV cirrhosis AND schistosomiasis make varices common.

weights.csoNote: This is a SEVERITY category — the haemodynamically-unstable presentation of ANY upper-GI bleed (usually variceal or peptic ulcer), not a distinct aetiology; it captures the RESUSCITATION imperative (ABC, transfuse, urgent endoscopy) and the Glasgow-Blatchford/Rockall risk tools. NOTE: Mallory-Weiss tear (haematemesis AFTER retching/vomiting, often alcohol-related, usually self-limiting) is the benign upper-GI cause to weigh against this — it is not separately tokenised; recommend a 'retching/vomiting preceded bleed' cue.
weights.weightCitation: NICE acute upper-GI bleeding (CG141); BSG acute UGIB care bundle; Glasgow-Blatchford score; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)

Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (colorectal carcinoma). PR bleeding + change in bowel habit + weight loss + iron-deficiency anaemia; left-sided -> PR bleeding/obstruction, right-sided -> occult anaemia. Pin for everyone — PR bleeding must never be attributed to haemorrhoids until cancer is excluded.

weights.csoNote: UNCOMMON in sub-Saharan populations (low AAA prevalence — hence basePrior 0 + conditional). Two entities: ruptured AAA (tearing abdominal/back pain + collapse) and AORTO-ENTERIC FISTULA (GI bleed in someone with a PRIOR AORTIC GRAFT — a 'herald' bleed precedes exsanguination). PIN GATED ON tearing/back pain OR prior aortic graft — deliberately NOT on plain 'abdominal pain' (near-universal in GI bleed → over-triggers) nor 'smoking' (weak); both kept as score weights only. CAPTURE GAP (adversarial-verified): 'prior aortic graft' is not yet a history token, so the aorto-enteric-fistula pin currently relies on tearing/back-pain capture — recommend adding a 'prior aortic graft' background item.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2014 Aortic Diseases Guideline; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (ruptured AAA / aorto-enteric fistula)

NICE/BSG acute UGIB; Maastricht VI H. pylori consensus; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022). The commonest cause of upper-GI bleeding — melaena +/- haematemesis with epigastric/postprandial pain; drivers are H. pylori (NOT tokenised — recommend adding) and NSAIDs; PPI + endoscopy + H. pylori eradication.

Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (haemorrhoids / diverticular bleeding). Bright-red PR bleeding (on the paper/coating stool) WITHOUT weight loss or bowel-habit change suggests haemorrhoids — but only after colorectal malignancy is excluded (esp with weight loss/bowel change/anaemia). Diverticular disease is less common in SSA.

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on haematemesis/exposure. UGANDA: S. mansoni (Lake Victoria/Albert) -> Symmers' PERIPORTAL FIBROSIS -> PRESINUSOIDAL portal hypertension -> oesophageal varices — a MAJOR cause of variceal bleeding in YOUNG patients WITHOUT cirrhosis. KEY DISTINCTION from cirrhotic varices: PRESERVED liver function (NO jaundice, NO early ascites, often massive splenomegaly) — hence the NEGATIVE jaundice weight. The freshwater/lake-contact exposure is only loosely 'high-risk exposure' — recommend a specific token.
weights.weightCitation: WHO schistosomiasis guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Symmers' periportal fibrosis -> presinusoidal portal hypertension)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on weight loss/known cancer. UGANDA/East Africa: OESOPHAGEAL cancer (squamous) is notably common (the East-African 'oesophageal cancer corridor'); gastric adenocarcinoma (H. pylori-related). Presents with DYSPHAGIA (not cleanly tokenised — recommend adding) + weight loss + chronic upper-GI bleeding / iron-deficiency anaemia. PIN tightened to weight loss OR known cancer — 'smoking' removed from the pin (weak discriminator, kept as a score weight). CAPTURE GAP (adversarial-verified): H. pylori — a primary driver — is not tokenised; recommend adding it as a background/risk item. Endoscopy + biopsy.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022); WHO cancer (oesophageal cancer, East Africa)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on fever. UGANDA: typhoid (Salmonella Typhi) is endemic; in the 3RD WEEK, terminal-ileal ulceration causes GI BLEEDING or PERFORATION (a surgical emergency with peritonitis) — the classic complication. Sustained fever + abdominal pain + GI bleed. Contaminated-water/food exposure is only loosely 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO typhoid (enteric fever) guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (terminal-ileal perforation/bleeding, week 3)

weights.csoNote: UGANDA: high TB burden — ileocaecal/abdominal TB is an important mimic of CROHN'S disease and CAECAL CANCER (chronic fever, night sweats, weight loss, RIF mass, altered bowel habit). GI bleeding is a LESS-dominant feature than obstruction/mass/perforation, so marked 'likely' for the bleeding complaint; needs tissue/ascitic diagnosis (don't start empirical anti-TB blindly).
weights.weightCitation: WHO Consolidated TB Guidelines; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (ileocaecal/abdominal TB)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on HIV/immunosuppression. UGANDA: Kaposi sarcoma (HHV-8) is common in advanced HIV and an AIDS-defining malignancy; GI KS lesions cause bleeding (often OCCULT/chronic, occasionally brisk) and usually accompany cutaneous/oral/palatal KS. Endoscopy; ART + chemotherapy.
weights.weightCitation: WHO HIV / opportunistic-infection guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (Kaposi sarcoma, HHV-8)

weights.csoNote: Bloody diarrhoea + fever + tenesmus/cramps — BACILLARY (Shigella — can be severe/epidemic) or AMOEBIC (Entamoeba histolytica — can cause liver abscess and colonic perforation). Common in Uganda; the blood is MIXED with frequent loose motions (distinct from the isolated PR bleeding of haemorrhoids/cancer). Stool microscopy; treat (cipro/azithro for Shigella; metronidazole for amoebic). Contaminated-water/food exposure only loosely 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO guidance (Shigella / amoebiasis); Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (dysentery)

weights.dx: Hookworm / helminth chronic occult blood loss
weights.csoNote: The OCCULT/CHRONIC blood-loss category. UGANDA: hookworm (and other helminths) cause chronic OCCULT intestinal blood loss -> IRON-DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA — presenting with PALLOR/FATIGUE/dyspnoea, NOT visible bleeding (hence NEGATIVE weights on haematemesis/melaena/PR-bleeding). Very common; stool microscopy + FBC/iron studies; deworm + iron. Soil/barefoot exposure only loosely 'high-risk exposure'.
weights.weightCitation: WHO soil-transmitted helminths guidance; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (hookworm iron-deficiency anaemia)

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on bleeding disorder/liver disease/anticoagulant/easy-bruising. Bleeding from a COAGULOPATHY rather than a single lesion — liver failure (low clotting factors), DIC (sepsis, severe malaria, obstetric), over-anticoagulation (warfarin/DOAC), thrombocytopenia; bleeding from MULTIPLE sites + easy bruising. Check FBC/platelets, INR/PT, fibrinogen. ACTIVE-OUTBREAK NOTE: a coagulopathy with FEVER + BLEEDING + high-risk exposure within 21 days must trigger Viral Haemorrhagic Fever precautions — see the dedicated VHF entry.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022) (liver failure / DIC); ISTH DIC criteria

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL on high-risk exposure. ACTIVE OUTBREAK (web-verified this session): a WHO-declared PHEIC of BUNDIBUGYO virus disease (a species of Ebola) is ongoing in Uganda & DRC as of June 2026, with confirmed Uganda cases including Mulago's catchment (Kampala/Wakiso). GI BLEEDING (haematemesis/melaena/PR) is a haemorrhagic manifestation. A compatible febrile bleeding illness + epidemiological risk within 21 days = VHF UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE -> ISOLATE + NOTIFY public health immediately; do NOT perform non-essential procedures/endoscopy until excluded. Re-review the suspect-case definition + outbreak weighting against the live WHO/Uganda MoH situation. The 21-day exposure window is not precisely tokenised ('high-risk exposure' is the proxy). PIN GATED ON EXPOSURE ONLY (not fever alone — fever+GI-bleed is usually typhoid/dysentery; matches the fever-pack VHF entry).
weights.weightCitation: WHO Ebola & Marburg guidance; WHO Disease Outbreak News — Bundibugyo virus disease, DRC/Uganda (2026, web-verified this session); Uganda MoH; Davidson's Principles & Practice of Medicine 24th ed (2022)
